question: When the player fought the Hundred-Eyed Daoist Master (百目真人), which of the following skills were used? 1. Wandering Wight (幽魂) Spirit (精魄) 2. Out-of-Body Movement 3. Immobilize (定身术) 4. Rock Solid (铜头铁臂)

rollouts.answer: 3. Immobilize + 4. Rock Solid, citing evidence at ~50,520-50,550s
rollouts.tool_call_sequence: read_skill x3 -> semantic_search(episodes/visual_clips/entities/topic_facts) -> run_sql(episodes/visual_clips/topic_facts/event_steps @13000-14000) -> semantic_search x3 more -> run_sql(topic_facts LIKE skill-name terms) -> run_sql(episodes/topic_facts/visual_clips/event_steps @14900-16400, includes the true clue window 15090-15150) -> run_sql(entities LIKE 百目) -> semantic_search(event_steps/visual_clips) -> run_sql(episodes/topic_facts/event_steps/visual_clips @50500-51050) -> run_sql(topic_facts @55000-56000) -> submit (no clip_qa ever called)

run_sql on topic_facts 50500-51050 returned an explicit text fact 'player uses skills 定身, 聚形散气, 铜头铁臂' at 50520s against an unrelated 'large horned creature' encounter; the agent equated this readable skill-name text with the target boss fight purely because it was legible, without ever confirming via entity/name search that this encounter is 百目真人.

rollouts.failure_point: Correct evidence window (15090-15150) was retrieved into context via a broad SQL range query but never visually verified with clip_qa; the agent instead substituted a textually convenient but wrong encounter (50520s, different enemy) because it explicitly named skills in the OCR text, and never cross-checked entity identity against the boss name.
rollouts.evidence_checked: Confirmed via sql that visual_clips:000503/000504 (15090-15150) are in fact the clue window, and via frame extraction at 15106/15112 that the boss health-bar label there reads 百目真人.

db_evidence.notes: The correct fight footage (visual_clips:000503/000504, 15090-15150s) is retrievable via straightforward time-window SQL/semantic search over episodes/visual_clips, and several rollouts did pull it into context (rollout 0 explicitly, rollout 3 via a 12000-16000 range query). However, no table anywhere tags this specific 4-8s clue window with the boss name '百目真人' or with explicit skill names -- the only DB text confirming the boss identity is topic_facts/episodes at 15180 ('purple enemy marker...面目真人') and 15210 ('skill menu...百目真人'), i.e. slightly AFTER the clue window, and entities table has no row for 百目真人 at all (confirmed empty via SQL). Frame extraction at 15106/15112 confirms via the in-game boss health-bar label ('百目真人') that this is indeed the correct fight, and at 15112 the player is visually in a transformed blue/grey creature state consistent with 'Wandering Wight spirit'. So the clue is retrievable in principle by combining the 15090-15150 combat description with the 15180-15210 name confirmation, but requires a clip_qa call on the correct window that none of the 5 rollouts made; instead all 5 clip_qa calls (rollouts 1-4) went to an unconfirmed decoy encounter at 13200-13290 that only superficially matches on 'multiple eyes'.

root_causes: Missing/late entity linkage: the entities table has no row for 百目真人 (boss), so there is no anchor row from which to jump straight to its exact appearance interval; the boss name only exists in OCR'd topic_facts/episodes text slightly after the true clue window (15180-15210), never inside 15090-15150 itself.

Visual-keyword decoy: a genuinely different boss encounter at ~13200-13290 is independently described as having 'multiple glowing yellow eyes and webbed spider-like body', which 4 of 5 rollouts semantically pattern-matched to 'Hundred-Eyed' without any textual name confirmation, then anchored their only clip_qa call there.

Leading/biased clip_qa questions: every clip_qa call that targeted the decoy window stated as fact 'this is the fight against the Hundred-Eyed Daoist Master (百目真人)' in the question text, priming the visual sub-agent to answer within that false frame rather than to verify boss identity.

Broad SQL range queries did surface the true clue window (rollouts 0 and 3) but the main agent did not follow up with a targeted clip_qa there, instead trusting whichever region had the most legible on-screen skill-name text (rollout 0 substituted an unrelated 50520s encounter) or continuing to explore the decoy region (rollout 3).
No rollout cross-referenced the boss-name-confirmed interval (15180-15210, from topic_facts) backward to the immediately preceding combat clip (15090-15150) to trigger a visual check there.
what_worked: All 5 rollouts correctly executed the general retrieval workflow (skill read-in, semantic_search across multiple tables, SQL time-window scans, clip_qa for visual confirmation) and all landed on subset {3,4}, {3}, {1,4}, or {3,4} rather than random guesses -- showing the retrieval loop functions and does find real (but wrong-location) skill-use footage.

Rollout 0 and rollout 3's broad SQL time-window queries (14900-16400 and 12000-16000 respectively) did technically retrieve the correct clue window into the agent's context, showing that the underlying database content is discoverable with plain range queries.
transferable_lessons: Before trusting a visual-keyword match (e.g. 'multiple eyes') as evidence of a named entity, cross-check that the same time region (or an immediately adjacent bin) also contains the entity's name in OCR'd text/topic_facts/entities; do not let a clip_qa question assert the boss identity as a given premise.

When a broad SQL range query returns dozens of rows, do not skip past the correct answer's bin just because a later bin was easier to read; explicitly scan all bins in the returned range for the target entity's name or attributes before moving to a different time window.

When the entities table lacks a row for a named boss, search topic_facts/episodes text for the exact bilingual name and use the interval immediately BEFORE the first confirmed name-mention as a candidate for the actual combat footage (games routinely show the boss nameplate mid-fight and menus/loot popups after the fight ends).

Always issue at least one clip_qa call on the literal timestamp interval implied by upstream entity/name evidence, even if a decoy region looks visually more distinctive -- do not substitute a textually convenient but unconfirmed encounter for the target.
open_questions: Whether earlier compaction/context limits in rollout 0's long segment (9 LLM calls, up to ~91k input tokens) caused it to lose track of the 15090-15150 window it had already retrieved by the time it reached the 50520 window later in the same trace.

Whether the game actually shows a distinct 'Rock Solid' or 'Out-of-Body' animation in the 15090-15150 window that would change the reference answer's completeness; only frames at 15106/15112/15113 were inspected here, not the full 15090-15150 range.
